name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes—critical for power tasks—while running fast enough to avoid bottlenecking the workflow. The trade-off is its GPU memory footprint, but EXCAVA’s current setup can handle it without extra cost.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—it’s a scene-level tool, not a face-level one. RealVisXL’s face model locks us into another proprietary black box—its "late" updates break backward compatibility. Test both on a controlled face-focused prompt set; if neither gains ≥0.5% fidelity, pivot to open-source face-specific upscalers like FaceDetailer or GFPGAN—both run in EXCAVA’s pipeline without new dependencies.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s latest face reconstruction model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. The trade-off is locking into a proprietary model that may update unpredictably, but EXCAVA’s current face prompts demand this specificity; we’ll mitigate risk by freezing the model version in the pipeline.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s "latest" face model is a moving target—its backward compatibility claims are marketing, not engineering. The real risk isn’t just lock-in; it’s that every update could silently degrade EXCAVA’s output without warning. Test it against a static reference set of 50 controlled face prompts, then compare against an open alternative like *FaceChain’s* reconstruction model—if neither moves the needle by 0.5%+, default to the open option.
